classifications.reason: Human propulsion does not rule out an electric motor, but the bicycle contract does not establish the required motor, handlebars or riding design.
Design for carrying many passengers supplies no contractual weight or speed bound that makes the quoted limits exclude every bus.
The admitting words describe a device, whereas the child contract describes a pedestrian person rather than such a device.
The commercial-licensing alternative neither establishes nor conflicts with the required device features, and the contracts guarantee no complete coverage by an included class.
An assisting electric motor does not establish the full handlebar-and-riding-design description, and no clause excludes electric bicycles as a class.

The admitting clause matches the class's handlebar-equipped standing-or-seated electric-scooter design, subject to the stated limits, and the exception describes an assistive purpose not specified by this class's contract.
Emergency designation neither establishes nor conflicts with the required device features, and the contracts do not guarantee that every qualifying member carries an included covering class.
A fire-fighting purpose supplies no contractual weight or speed bound that necessarily violates either quoted limit.
The moped contract permits an electric motor without establishing all required features or violating the quoted limits, and no exception removes mopeds as a class.
Self-propulsion entails neither exceeding the quoted limits nor belonging exclusively to the separately classed powered two-wheelers that the contract excludes.
The motorcycle contract supplies neither a necessary conflict with the weight and speed limits nor all the features needed for admission, and no exception names motorcycles.
Official road service and identifying equipment neither establish nor conflict with the required device features, and the contracts guarantee no complete coverage by an included class.
The definition admits devices, while the pedestrian contract describes a person on foot or using a device rather than the device itself.
The contract describes a pedestrian person with specified assistance, not a device admitted by the definition.
Being on-track does not contractually preclude handlebars, an electric motor or the specified riding design, so the quoted clause establishes no class-wide exclusion.
School-bus designation and markings establish no weight or speed bound that necessarily violates the quoted limits.
Passenger service for hire and identifying markings establish neither a minimum weight above one hundred pounds nor a motor-only maximum speed above twenty miles per hour.
The tour, shuttle and lengthened-passenger-vehicle descriptions provide no contractual weight or speed bound that excludes every member under the quoted limits.
The contract includes combinations, and the quoted words do not establish that every such combination lacks handlebars, electric propulsion or the required riding design.
Public-transit service and identifying displays establish no weight or speed bound that necessarily violates the quoted limits.
A body built for carrying goods establishes no contractual minimum weight or motor-only maximum speed incompatible with the quoted limits.
